tool_mode_token_benchmark.command: npm run bench:modes (also embedded in npm run bench:mcp as `modes`)
tool_mode_token_benchmark.method: Three real MCP stdio servers, one per VENIRA_TOOL_MODE, each on its own copy of the same five-file fixture. Same task in every mode: read five files, add a `// touched` line to each, run `echo refactor-ok`. default/core use read_file batch + edit_file batch + shell_run (3 turns); minimal uses one execute_js snippet with venira.read/venira.edit/venira.shell (1 turn).
tool_mode_token_benchmark.accounting: surface_bytes = instructions + tools/list JSON; call_bytes = serialized arguments of the reference plan; result_bytes = response text returned by those calls; tokens = ceil(bytes / 4). Context-cost estimate, not a tokenizer run; no model is called.
tool_mode_token_benchmark.task: refactor 5 files: read -> edit -> echo refactor-ok

ratios.note: Surface dominates: 84,784 B (default) vs 10,439 B (minimal); executed work is identical and all modes report task_ok.

audit_attribution.note: Phase 4 of ROADMAP_MINIMAL_MODE.md is covered by tests, not by a benchmark: scripts/test-audit-verify.ts pins that pre-migration (v2) rows still verify next to v3 rows that hash parent_call_id, and scripts/test-sdk-integration.ts pins that every op an execute_js snippet runs carries the execute_js request id and is returned by read_audit { parent_call_id }.
